The [[mathematics|mathematical]] statements discussed below are {{not a typo|provably}} [[independence (mathematical logic)|independent]] of [[ZFC]] (the canonical [[axiomatic set theory]] of contemporary mathematics, consisting of the [[Zermelo–Fraenkel axioms]] plus the [[axiom of choice]]), assuming that ZFC is [[consistent]]. A statement is independent of ZFC (sometimes phrased "undecidable in ZFC") if it can neither be proven nor disproven from the axioms of ZFC.

==Axiomatic set theory==
{{further|Axiomatic set theory}}
In 1931, [[Kurt Gödel]] proved his [[Gödel's second incompleteness theorem|incompleteness theorems]], establishing that many mathematical theories, including ZFC, cannot prove their own consistency. Assuming [[ω-consistency]] of such a theory, the consistency statement can also not be disproven, meaning it is independent. A few years later, other arithmetic statements were defined that are independent of any such theory, see for example [[Rosser's trick]]. 

The following set theoretic statements are independent of ZFC, among others:
* the [[continuum hypothesis]] or CH (Gödel produced a model of ZFC in which CH is true, showing that CH cannot be disproven in ZFC; [[Paul Cohen (mathematician)|Paul Cohen]] later invented the method of [[forcing (mathematics)|forcing]] to exhibit a model of ZFC in which CH fails, showing that CH cannot be proven in ZFC. The following four independence results are also due to Gödel/Cohen.);
* the [[generalized continuum hypothesis]] (GCH); 
* a related independent statement is that if a set ''x'' has fewer elements than ''y'', then ''x'' also has fewer [[subset]]s than ''y''. In particular, this statement fails when the cardinalities of the power sets of ''x'' and ''y'' coincide;
* the [[axiom of constructibility]] (''V'' = ''L''); 
* the [[diamond principle]] (◊);
* [[Martin's axiom]] (MA);
* MA + ¬CH (independence shown by [[Robert Solovay|Solovay]] and [[Stanley Tennenbaum|Tennenbaum]]).<ref>{{cite book| last=Kunen |first=Kenneth |author-link= Kenneth Kunen|title=[[Set Theory: An Introduction to Independence Proofs]]|publisher=Elsevier|year=1980|isbn=0-444-86839-9}}</ref>
* Every [[Aronszajn tree]] is special (EATS);

[[File:Implication Chains of Undecidable ZFC Statements.png|thumbnail|Diagram showing the implication chains]]

We have the following chains of implications:
:''V'' = ''L'' → ◊ → CH,
:''V'' = ''L'' → GCH → CH,
:CH → MA,
and (see section on order theory):
:◊ → ¬[[Suslin hypothesis|SH]],
:MA + ¬CH → EATS → SH.

Several statements related to the existence of [[large cardinal]]s cannot be proven in ZFC (assuming ZFC is consistent). These are independent of ZFC provided that they are consistent with ZFC, which most working set theorists believe to be the case. These statements are strong enough to imply the consistency of ZFC. This has the consequence (via [[Gödel's incompleteness theorem|Gödel's second incompleteness theorem]]) that their consistency with ZFC cannot be proven in ZFC (assuming ZFC is consistent). The following statements belong to this class:
* Existence of [[inaccessible cardinal]]s
* Existence of [[Mahlo cardinal]]s
* Existence of [[measurable cardinal]]s (first conjectured by [[Stanislaw Ulam|Ulam]])
* Existence of [[supercompact cardinal]]s

The following statements can be proven to be independent of ZFC assuming the consistency of a suitable large cardinal:
* [[Proper forcing axiom]]
* [[Open coloring axiom]]
* [[Martin's maximum]]
* Existence of [[zero sharp|0<sup>#</sup>]]
* [[Singular cardinals hypothesis]]
* [[Projective determinacy]] (and even the full [[axiom of determinacy]] if the [[axiom of choice]] is not assumed)

==Set theory of the real line==
{{further|Set theory of the real line}}
There are many [[cardinal invariant]]s of the real line, connected with [[measure theory]] and statements related to the [[Baire category theorem]], whose exact values are independent of ZFC. While nontrivial relations can be proved between them, most cardinal invariants can be any [[regular cardinal]] between [[Aleph number#Aleph-one|ℵ<sub>1</sub>]] and [[Cardinality of the continuum|2<sup>ℵ<sub>0</sub></sup>]]. This is a major area of study in the set theory of the real line (see [[Cichon diagram]]). MA has a tendency to set most interesting cardinal invariants equal to 2<sup>ℵ<sub>0</sub></sup>.

A subset ''X'' of the real line is a [[strong measure zero set]] if to every sequence (''ε<sub>n</sub>'') of positive reals there exists a sequence of intervals ({{mvar|I<sub>n</sub>}}) which covers ''X'' and such that {{mvar|I<sub>n</sub>}} has length at most ''ε<sub>n</sub>''. Borel's conjecture, that every strong measure zero set is countable, is independent of ZFC.

A subset ''X'' of the real line is <math>\aleph_1</math>-dense if every open interval contains <math>\aleph_1</math>-many elements of ''X''. Whether all <math>\aleph_1</math>-dense sets are order-isomorphic is independent of ZFC.<ref>Baumgartner, J., All <math>\aleph_1</math>-dense sets of reals can be isomorphic, Fund. Math. 79, pp.101 – 106, 1973</ref>

==Order theory==
{{further|Order theory}}
[[Suslin's problem]] asks whether a specific short list of properties characterizes the ordered set of real numbers '''R'''. This is undecidable in ZFC.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Iterated Cohen extensions and Souslin's problem|last=Solovay|first=R. M.|author2=Tennenbaum, S. |journal=Annals of Mathematics |series=Second Series|volume=94|issue=2|year=1971|pages=201–245|doi=10.2307/1970860|jstor=1970860}}</ref> A ''Suslin line'' is an ordered set which satisfies this specific list of properties but is not order-isomorphic to '''R'''. The [[diamond principle]] ◊ proves the existence of a Suslin line, while MA + ¬CH implies EATS ([[every Aronszajn tree is special]]),<ref>Baumgartner, J., J. Malitz, and W. Reiehart, Embedding trees in the rationals, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A., 67, pp. 1746 – 1753, 1970</ref> which in turn implies (but is not equivalent to)<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Shelah | first1=S.
| title=Free limits of forcing and more on Aronszajn trees
| journal=[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]
| volume=38
| pages=315–334
| year=1981
| issue=4
| doi=10.1007/BF02762777 | doi-access=free}}</ref> the nonexistence of Suslin lines. [[Ronald Jensen]] proved that CH does not imply the existence of a Suslin line.<ref>Devlin, K., and H. Johnsbraten, The Souslin Problem, Lecture Notes on Mathematics 405, Springer, 1974</ref>

Existence of [[Kurepa tree]]s is independent of ZFC, assuming consistency of an [[inaccessible cardinal]].<ref>Silver, J., The independence of Kurepa's conjecture and two-cardinal conjectures in model theory, in Axiomatic Set Theory, Proc. Symp, in Pure Mathematics (13) pp. 383 – 390, 1967</ref>

Existence of a partition of the [[ordinal number]] <math>\omega_2</math> into two colors with no monochromatic uncountable sequentially closed subset is independent of ZFC, ZFC + CH, and ZFC + ¬CH, assuming consistency of a [[Mahlo cardinal]].<ref>Shelah, S., Proper and Improper Forcing, Springer 1992</ref><ref>Schlindwein, Chaz, Shelah's work on non-semiproper iterations I, Archive for Mathematical Logic (47) 2008 pp. 579 – 606</ref><ref>Schlindwein, Chaz, Shelah's work on non-semiproper iterations II, Journal of Symbolic Logic (66) 2001, pp. 1865 – 1883</ref>  This theorem of [[Saharon Shelah|Shelah]] answers a question of [[Harvey Friedman (mathematician)|H. Friedman]].

==Abstract algebra==
{{further|Abstract algebra}}
In 1973, [[Saharon Shelah]] showed that the [[Whitehead problem]] ("is every [[abelian group]] ''A'' with [[ext functor|Ext]]<sup>1</sup>(A, '''Z''') = 0 a [[free abelian group]]?") is independent of ZFC.<ref>{{cite journal|mr=0357114| first=S.|last=Shelah|title=Infinite Abelian groups, Whitehead problem and some constructions
|journal=[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]] |volume=18 |year=1974| issue=3|pages=243–256|doi=10.1007/BF02757281|doi-access=free}}</ref> An abelian group with Ext<sup>1</sup>(A, '''Z''') = 0 is called a Whitehead group; [[Martin's Axiom|MA]] + ¬CH proves the existence of a non-free Whitehead group, while ''V'' = ''L'' proves that all Whitehead groups are free.
In one of the earliest applications of proper [[forcing (mathematics)|forcing]], Shelah constructed a model of ZFC + CH in which there is a non-free Whitehead group.<ref>{{Cite journal 
| last1=Shelah | first1=S.
| title=Whitehead groups may be not free, even assuming CH, I
| journal=[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]
| volume=28
| pages=193–204
| year=1972
| issue=3
| doi=10.1007/BF02759809 | doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Shelah | first1=S.
| title=Whitehead groups may not be free even assuming CH, II
| journal=[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]
| volume=35
| pages=257–285
| year=1980
| issue=4
| doi=10.1007/BF02760652 | doi-access=free}}</ref>

A few years earlier, [[Barbara L. Osofsky|Barbara Osofsky]] had proved several independence results, including: 

* Consider the ring ''A'' = '''R'''[''x'',''y'',''z''] of [[Polynomial ring|polynomials]] in three variables over the real numbers and its [[field of fractions]] ''M'' = '''R'''(''x'',''y'',''z''). The [[projective dimension]] of ''M'' as ''A''-module is 2 if the continuum hypothesis holds and 3 if it doesn't hold.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Barbara L. Osofsky|author-link=Barbara L. Osofsky|title=Homological dimension and the continuum hypothesis|journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society|year=1968|volume=132|pages=217–230|url= https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/1968-132-01/S0002-9947-1968-0224606-4/S0002-9947-1968-0224606-4.pdf | doi = 10.1090/s0002-9947-1968-0224606-4 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

* If the continuum hypothesis holds, then every ring that's a [[direct product]] of countably many [[field (mathematics)|field]]s has [[global dimension]] 2; if the continuum hypothesis does not hold, then each such ring has global dimension greater than 2.<ref name="oso">{{cite book |title=Homological Dimensions of Modules|author=Barbara L. Osofsky|author-link=Barbara L. Osofsky|publisher=American Mathematical Soc.|year=1973|page=60 |isbn=978-0-8218-1662-2|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=rTTS6seRfSIC&q=Homological+Dimensions+of+Modules}}</ref>

==Number theory==
{{further|Number theory}}
One can write down a concrete polynomial ''p'' ∈ '''Z'''[''x''<sub>1</sub>, ..., ''x''<sub>9</sub>] such that the statement "there are integers ''m''<sub>1</sub>, ..., ''m''<sub>9</sub> with ''p''(''m''<sub>1</sub>, ..., ''m''<sub>9</sub>) = 0" can neither be proven nor disproven in ZFC (assuming ZFC is consistent).  This follows from [[Yuri Matiyasevich]]'s resolution of [[Hilbert's tenth problem]]; the polynomial is constructed so that it has an integer root if and only if ZFC is inconsistent.<ref>See e.g.: 
* {{cite journal|author=James P. Jones|title=Undecidable diophantine equations|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.| volume=3 |number=2|year=1980|pages=859–862|url=http://projecteuclid.org/download/pdf_1/euclid.bams/1183547548|doi=10.1090/s0273-0979-1980-14832-6|doi-access=free}}
* {{cite journal|last1=Carl|first1=M.|last2=Moroz|first2=B.|title=On a Diophantine Representation of the Predicate of Provability|journal=Journal of Mathematical Sciences|issue=199|year=2014|volume=199|pages=36–52|doi=10.1007/s10958-014-1830-2|hdl=21.11116/0000-0004-1E89-1|s2cid=34618563|hdl-access=free}}  
For a summary of the argument, see {{slink|Hilbert's tenth problem|Applications}}.</ref>

==Measure theory==
{{further|Measure theory}}
A stronger version of [[Fubini's theorem]] for positive functions, where the function is no longer assumed to be [[measurable]] but merely that the two iterated integrals are well defined and exist, is independent of ZFC. On the one hand, CH implies that there exists a function on the unit square whose iterated integrals are not equal — the function is simply the [[indicator function]] of an ordering of [0, 1] equivalent to a [[well ordering]] of the cardinal ω<sub>1</sub>. A similar example can be constructed using [[Martin's axiom|MA]]. On the other hand, the consistency of the strong Fubini theorem was first shown by [[Harvey Friedman (mathematician)|Friedman]].<ref>{{cite journal |first=Harvey |last=Friedman |year=1980 |title=A Consistent Fubini-Tonelli Theorem for Nonmeasurable Functions |journal=Illinois J. Math. |volume=24 |issue=3 |pages=390–395 |doi=10.1215/ijm/1256047607 |mr=573474 |doi-access=free }}</ref> It can also be deduced from a variant of [[Freiling's axiom of symmetry]].<ref>{{cite journal |author-link=Chris Freiling |first=Chris |last=Freiling |year=1986 |title=Axioms of symmetry: throwing darts at the real number line |journal=[[Journal of Symbolic Logic]] |volume=51 |issue=1 |pages=190–200 |mr=830085 |jstor=2273955 |doi=10.2307/2273955|s2cid=38174418 }}</ref>

==Topology==
{{further|Topology}}
The Normal Moore Space conjecture, namely that every [[normal space|normal]] [[Moore space (topology)|Moore space]] is [[metrizable space|metrizable]], can be disproven assuming the [[continuum hypothesis]] or assuming both [[Martin's axiom]] and the negation of the continuum hypothesis, and can be proven assuming a certain axiom which implies the existence of [[large cardinal]]s. Thus, granted large cardinals, the Normal Moore Space conjecture is independent of ZFC.<ref>{{cite book
 | last = Nyikos | first = Peter J.
 | contribution = A history of the normal Moore space problem
 | doi = 10.1007/978-94-017-0470-0_7
 | isbn = 0-7923-6970-X
 | location = Dordrecht
 | mr = 1900271
 | pages = 1179–1212
 | publisher = Kluwer Academic Publishers
 | title = Handbook of the History of General Topology
 | series = History of Topology
 | volume = 3
 | year = 2001}}</ref>

The existence of an [[S-space]] is independent of ZFC. In particular, it is implied by the existence of a Suslin line.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Todorcevic |first1=Stevo |title=Partition problems in topology |date=1989 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |location=Providence, R.I. |isbn=978-0-8218-5091-6}}</ref>

==Functional analysis==
{{further|Functional analysis}}
[[Garth Dales]] and [[Robert M. Solovay]] proved in 1976 that [[Kaplansky's conjecture]], namely that every [[algebra homomorphism]] from the [[Banach algebra]] ''C''(''X'') (where ''X'' is some [[compact space|compact]] [[Hausdorff space]]) into any other Banach algebra must be continuous, is independent of ZFC. CH implies that for any infinite ''X'' there exists a discontinuous homomorphism into any Banach algebra.<ref>{{cite book|author=H. G. Dales |author2=W. H. Woodin |title=An introduction to independence for analysts|year=1987}}</ref>

Consider the algebra ''B''(''H'') of [[bounded operator|bounded linear operator]]s on the infinite-dimensional [[Hilbert space#Separable spaces|separable]] [[Hilbert space]] ''H''. The [[compact operator]]s form a two-sided ideal in ''B''(''H''). The question of whether this ideal is the sum of two properly smaller ideals is independent of ZFC, as was proved by [[Andreas Blass]] and [[Saharon Shelah]] in 1987.<ref>{{cite journal| title= The Uses of Set Theory|author=Judith Roitman|journal=Mathematical Intelligencer|year=1992|volume=14|number=1}}</ref>

[[Charles Akemann]] and [[Nik Weaver]] showed in 2003 that the statement "there exists a counterexample to [[Naimark's problem]] which is generated by ℵ<sub>1</sub>, elements" is independent of ZFC.

Miroslav Bačák and [[Petr Hájek (mathematician, functional analysis)|Petr Hájek]] proved in 2008 that the statement "every [[Asplund space]] of density character ω<sub>1</sub> has a renorming with the [[Mazur intersection property]]" is independent of ZFC. The result is shown using [[Martin's maximum]] axiom, while Mar Jiménez and José Pedro Moreno (1997) had presented a counterexample assuming CH.

As shown by [[Ilijas Farah]]<ref>{{cite journal
| first=Ilijas | last=Farah
| year=2011
| title=All automorphisms of the Calkin algebra are inner
| journal=Annals of Mathematics
| series=Second Series
| volume=173
| issue=2
| pages=619–661
| doi=10.4007/annals.2011.173.2.1 | doi-access=free
| arxiv=0705.3085}}</ref> and [[N. Christopher Phillips]] and [[Nik Weaver]],<ref>{{cite journal |first1=N. C. |last1=Phillips |first2=N. |last2=Weaver |title= The Calkin algebra has outer automorphisms |journal=[[Duke Mathematical Journal]] |volume=139 |issue=1 |pages=185–202 |year=2007 |doi=10.1215/S0012-7094-07-13915-2 |arxiv=math/0606594 |s2cid=13873756 }}</ref> the existence of outer automorphisms of the [[Calkin algebra]] depends on set theoretic assumptions beyond ZFC.

[[Wetzel's problem]], which asks if every set of [[analytic functions]] which takes at most countably many distinct values at every point is necessarily countable, is true if and only if the continuum hypothesis is false.<ref>{{cite journal
 | last = Erdős | first = P.
 | journal = The Michigan Mathematical Journal
 | mr = 0168482
 | pages = 9–10
 | title = An interpolation problem associated with the continuum hypothesis
 | url = http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.mmj/1028999028
 | volume = 11
 | year = 1964
 | doi=10.1307/mmj/1028999028| doi-access = free
 }}.</ref>

==Model theory==
{{further|Model theory}}
[[Chang's conjecture]] is independent of ZFC assuming the consistency of an [[Erdős cardinal]].

==Computability theory==
{{further|Computability theory}}
[[Marcia Groszek]] and [[Theodore Slaman]] gave examples of statements independent of ZFC concerning the structure of the Turing degrees. In particular, whether there exists a maximally independent set of degrees of size less than continuum.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=Marcia J. |last1=Groszek | author1-link = Marcia Groszek |first2=T. |last2=Slaman | author2-link = Theodore Slaman |title=Independence results on the global structure of the Turing degrees |journal=[[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]] |year=1983 |doi=10.2307/1999225 |volume=277 |issue=2 |page=579|jstor=1999225 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Numerical values of the [[busy beaver]] function are known to be independent of ZFC, such as BB(748). This is done by constructing a Turing machine with 748 states which halts if and only if there is an inconsistency in ZFC. If ZFC is consistent, it cannot prove this machine halts. It therefore also cannot prove any theorem of the form "BB(748) < ''n"'' for any concrete natural number ''n.''<ref name=":62">{{Cite journal |last=Aaronson |first=Scott |date=2020-09-29 |title=The Busy Beaver Frontier |url=https://scottaaronson.com/papers/bb.pdf |journal=SIGACT News |volume=51 |issue=3 |pages=32–54 |doi=10.1145/3427361.3427369 |issn=0163-5700 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220705224204/https://www.scottaaronson.com/papers/bb.pdf |archive-date=2022-07-05}}</ref>
